query: For structural materials intended for fusion plasma-facing components, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs high-temperature plastic strain and toughness, and why? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations predicted relative to an unperturbed baseline, the boundaries within which the hypothesis should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Rhenium atoms in tungsten reduce the Peierls barrier for screw dislocation motion by lowering the activation energy for kink‐pair nucleation, thereby increasing dislocation mobility at elevated temperatures and enhancing plastic strain and fracture toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: Pure polycrystalline tungsten, ~20 µm grain size, recrystallized, minimal residual stress
generation.intervention: Alloying with 3 at% rhenium under identical thermomechanical processing
generation.conditions: Uniaxial tensile and fracture toughness tests at 800 °C in inert atmosphere
generation.structural_mediator: Reduced Peierls stress for screw dislocations (quantified via activation energy for kink‐pair formation)
generation.mechanism: Local electronic interaction of Re atoms with the W lattice lowers lattice friction on screw dislocations, enabling sustained high‐temperature dislocation glide and crack‐tip blunting
generation.predicted_outcome: W–3Re shows ≥50% higher uniform elongation and ≥20% higher fracture toughness (K_IC) at 800 °C compared to pure W
generation.baseline: Pure W with uniform elongation ≈2% and K_IC ≈10 MPa·√m at 800 °C
generation.boundary: Valid for Re content ∼1–5 at% and temperatures between 700 °C and 1200 °C; outside these ranges other mechanisms may dominate
generation.uncertainty: Improvement magnitude may vary ±20% due to grain‐size, texture, and residual‐stress differences

falsification_experiment.design: Compare pure W and W–3Re specimens drawn from the same ingot (matched grain size and heat treatment); perform stress‐relaxation tests to extract activation energy for plastic flow, uniaxial tensile tests for uniform elongation, and fracture toughness tests at 800 °C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If W–3Re does not lower the activation energy by ≥5% and does not improve uniform elongation or fracture toughness beyond experimental uncertainties (±10% elongation, ±15% toughness), the hypothesis is falsified.
